transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-13
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Liam Hart (Redwood AE), Sofia Kim (Redwood SE), Ravi Desai (Redwood Product), Jordan Lee (PraxisAI), Priya Menon (PraxisAI), Carlos Rivera (PraxisAI)

[00:00] Liam (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — audio ok?
[00:05] Jordan (PraxisAI): Yep, good here.
[00:10] Sofia (Redwood SE): Great. We'll run a focused walkthrough of Redwood's Console — specifically the consumption mapping views and per-route finance dashboards, and how that ties into Optimize suggestions. If anything, interrupt, ask for specifics, we know you have complex billing needs.
[00:30] Priya (PraxisAI): Sounds good. Our main goal is expense clarity and being able to show FinOps teams the route-level spend for chargebacks.
[00:40] Ravi (Redwood Product): I will highlight how the console maps token usage to routes and how caching/quantization suggestions reduce unit costs.

[02:15] Sofia: (screen share) Starting from the Console home — top-left is the usage summary card, you can filter by date ranges and routes. For Praxis you said you route by model + endpoint label?
[02:30] Jordan: Yeah, we have about 12 production routes: chat-assist, summarize, search-embed, legal-review, extraction, etc. Most heavy volume is search-embed and chat-assist.
[02:48] Sofia: Okay. So I'll pick the last 30 days. You'll see the time-series tokens and cost estimate column on the right. Note: cost estimate uses your account's pricing profile or Redwood public pricing if not set.
[03:05] Carlos (PraxisAI): Quick Q — can we import our committed Reserved capacity rates? Our finance team wants accurate cost reports.
[03:12] Liam: Yes, we support reserved/dedicated pricing inputs and will map reserved capacity to a per-token effective rate in the console. We'll show that in the billing export.

[05:00] Sofia: Now switching to the route breakdown. Each route has a card — requests, avg latency, tokens per request, and an estimated cost bucket. You can click into a route to see per-model usage and traffic split.
[05:22] Jordan: That per-model split is critical — we federate across gpt-like and open LLM variants.
[05:30] Sofia: Right — the Console normalizes model outputs to token counts and associates kernel/quantization profiles when available. Small note — the transcription here may show 'K V cache' sometimes in logs, that's the speech transcriber.

[08:40] Sofia: When you drill into the chat-assist route, you'll see a waterfall of costs: model inference, KV cache misses, and external tool calls. There's also a header for SLO violations and retry costs, which can add up.
[09:00] Priya: Is retry cost included by default? We had an incident where retries spiked over a weekend.
[09:08] Ravi: Yes, retries and fallbacks are tagged. We also surface the rollback/fallback events where we routed to a cheaper model variant. You can toggle including or excluding fallbacks in the finance view.

[12:10] Sofia: Now I'll open the 'Optimize suggestions' panel tied to that route. It shows recommended batching thresholds, cache TTL adjustments, and a quantization profile suggestion for your heavy models. For example, for chat-assist we suggest int8 quantization with a small eval for output fidelity — that estimate shows ~38% cost reduction at minimal latency impact.
[12:40] Jordan: How confident are those savings? Real workloads sometimes regress.
[12:45] Sofia: Good point. We generate a small calibration set using your recent prompts if you consent to upload them, and run a fidelity check. We also show the delta in tokens and expected latency with margin.

[15:30] Carlos: From infra — network egress and dedicated GPU costs sometimes dominate. Does the console separate infra cost vs Redwood service charge?
[15:42] Liam: Yes, you can split the cost columns: Redwood-managed charges, compute (GPU) estimate, and your cloud egress. For private deployments we accept your cloud billing inputs to show a blended unit cost.

[18:20] Sofia: I'll demo the ad-hoc export flow. You can export per-route daily CSV with fields: date, route_id, route_name, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, calls, avg_lat_ms, cost_estimate, note_tags. This feed is suitable for FinOps ingestion.
[18:45] Priya: Perfect. We need that to feed into our chargeback pipeline. Can we map route metadata to our internal cost centers?
[18:52] Liam: Yes, routes support custom tags. You can add cost_center: team_x and a routing tag will propagate into exports and dashboards.

[22:00] Sofia: Now, a quick live example — I'm toggling the 'simulate optimizations' button on chat-assist: it shows before/after usage and cost curves, and projected monthly savings. 
[22:20] Jordan: I like the simulation. Does it simulate latency percentiles or just average?
[22:27] Sofia: Both. We show p50/p95/p99 estimates. For p99-sensitive routes we recommend smaller batching and prioritized KV caching.

[25:30] Ravi: On the topic of security/compliance — Praxis asked about private deployments, KMS integration, and audit logs. The Console's audit trail logs route-level changes, rollout actions, and user-level policy events. We integrate with external KMS for key rotation and HSM for on-prem.
[25:50] Priya: And SSO? We need SAML + SCIM provisioning.
[25:55] Liam: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM are supported; RBAC roles can restrict dashboard access by route and export capability. We can also redact prompt content in logs to meet PII constraints.

[30:00] Sofia: Switching to anomaly detection — the Console surfaces sudden spikes in tokens or cost per route and suggests root causes (model switch, traffic burst, retry storms). Each anomaly card links to raw traces and the request samples.
[30:20] Carlos: Can we set custom alert thresholds to integrate with PagerDuty?
[30:25] Sofia: Absolutely. Alerts can be per-route and per-metric and have escalation policies.

[33:40] Jordan: Our procurement question — how does Redwood treat burst capacity for Dedicated customers? We may occasionally spike beyond reserved.
[33:52] Liam: We offer burst pools that can be enabled with pay-as-you-go outside the commit; you get configured fallbacks and capacity-based routing. The Console will show forecasted overage and suggested commit changes.

[36:10] Priya: For chargebacks, we need attribution down to minor functions — e.g., embeddings used inside search workflows. Can the route-aggregation handle nested calls?
[36:22] Sofia: Yes, we have nested-call attribution: the parent route records cost for child embeddings and either attributes to parent or splits via a configurable rule. You can choose attribution model per route.

[40:00] Ravi: Quick demo of the cost-snapshot view — you can compare two windows and show delta by route and by tag. Useful for monthly FinOps reviews.
[40:12] Priya: Can we embed that view into Confluence or BI tools?
[40:18] Liam: We provide an embeddable iframe and API endpoints for programmatic snapshots; there's also a scheduled report export to S3.

[45:00] Sofia: Now a short technical aside on cache behavior — KV cache hit-rate is visible per route, and the console shows estimated token savings from cache hits. For LLMs with long context, a 60% hit rate can lead to dramatic M-TTR reductions.
[45:20] Jordan: Does Redwood surface which prompts are safe to cache? We have some sensitive prompts we can't cache.
[45:28] Sofia: You can set cache exclusion patterns and mark routes as non-cacheable. Cache content can be set to encrypted at rest and tied to KMS scopes.

[50:10] Carlos: Any limitations on the billing export frequency? We need near-real-time for internal dashboards.
[50:20] Liam: Exports can be scheduled hourly or delivered via streaming webhook for near-real-time telemetry. The invoices are still daily/monthly but the analytics feed can be streamed.

[54:00] Priya: A couple of risk items — we need SOC 2 Type II and evidence of penetration testing for our vendor review.
[54:10] Ravi: We can share our SOC 2 documentation and recent pentest summary. I'll add that as a follow-up deliverable.

[56:30] Jordan: Okay, last area — the console shows simulated cost impact of policy changes (e.g., set maximum tokens per route or enforce fallback to cheaper model). Can those policies be applied automatically?
[56:45] Sofia: Yes, you can create routing policies with thresholds — e.g., when p95 latency > 1s, route to dedicated pool or cheaper model; or when monthly cost > budget, apply fallback. Those policies can be manual, scheduled, or automatic with approval hooks.

[58:00] Liam: Let's recap quickly: We'll send the per-route export sample, SOC 2 docs, and network diagram plus KMS notes. We proposed a pilot scoping call for 10/20. Jordan to share top 10 routes and traffic patterns. Anything else?
[58:20] Jordan: No, that covers it. Appreciate the live simulation.
[58:28] Priya: One ask — please include the example CSV schema in the follow-up email.
[58:34] Liam: Will do.
[60:00] Sofia: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with docs and next steps.
[61:30] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mislabels (e.g., "K V" vs "KV"), short filler words and overlapping talk captured as separate lines. Some proper nouns normalized.
notes: Demo focused on Console consumption mapping, per-route exports, Optimize suggestions (batching, quantization, cache), security/compliance checklist, and pilot next steps. Customer needs: route-level chargeback CSV, SSO/SAML, SOC2 evidence, private deployment notes (KMS), and pilot scoping.
summary: Redwood walked PraxisAI through Console's route-level usage and finance tooling. Key outcomes: Praxis requests per-route CSV export and SOC2 + private deployment docs; Redwood proposes pilot scoping week of 2026-10-20 and will send pricing and network/KMS materials. Action owners and deadlines captured.
